examTitle: AWS Certified Developer – Associate (DVA-C02) Sample Set

questions.question: A developer needs to store session state for a stateless web application so that any server behind a load balancer can retrieve it with single-digit millisecond latency. Which service is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: ElastiCache for Redis is an in-memory data store built for low-latency, shared session storage across multiple application servers. S3 and RDS have higher latency profiles for this use case, and Storage Gateway is for hybrid storage, not session state.

questions.question: A developer is hardcoding a database password inside a Lambda function's code. Which TWO changes should be made to follow AWS security best practices? (Select TWO)
options: Store the password in AWS Secrets Manager and retrieve it at runtime
Store the password in an environment variable encrypted with a customer managed AWS KMS key
Store the password in a public S3 bucket for easy access
Embed the password in the Lambda function's IAM role name
Log the password to CloudWatch Logs for auditing
questions.explanation: Secrets Manager and KMS-encrypted environment variables both keep the credential out of source code while allowing secure retrieval at runtime. Public buckets, IAM role names, and logs are all inappropriate and insecure places to store credentials.

questions.question: A team wants to deploy a new version of an application to an Amazon ECS service with zero downtime and the ability to automatically roll back if CloudWatch alarms indicate errors. Which deployment approach should they use?
options: Manually stop and start ECS tasks
Recreate the ECS cluster from a CloudFormation template
questions.explanation: CodeDeploy's blue/green deployment type for ECS shifts traffic to a new task set and can automatically roll back based on CloudWatch alarms, achieving zero downtime with safe rollback. The other options either cause downtime or lack automated rollback.
